sections.h2: How can I sell my Mableton house quickly?
sections.html:
Mableton owners can list with an agent, sell privately, or accept an as-is offer, and the deciding factors are repair cost, how soon you need to move, and how much of the sale price you want to keep after costs. Mableton is a city in south Cobb County that voters created by referendum on November 8, 2022, with its first council seated after a March 21, 2023 election.

The Census Bureau estimates 78,820 residents for July 1, 2025, with an April 2020 estimates base of 77,077. A city that size has plenty of buyers and plenty of competing listings, so condition and price carry most of the weight.

sections.h2: What does Census data show about Mableton homes?
sections.html:
For 2020 to 2024, the Census Bureau lists 29,109 households in Mableton, with 64.6 percent living in homes they own. The median owner-occupied home value is $313,100, median monthly owner costs with a mortgage are $1,777, and median gross rent is $1,472.

  • Median household income: $77,980 (2020 to 2024, in 2024 dollars)
  • Residents living in the same house a year earlier: 88.1 percent
  • Bachelor's degree or higher among adults 25 and over: 38.7 percent
  • Mean travel time to work: 30.7 minutes

Because 88.1 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, listings in established streets are usually owned by long-time residents.

sections.h2: Where is Mableton and what is its history?
sections.html:
Mableton lies about 15 miles west-northwest of Atlanta and about 20 miles from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport. The Chattahoochee River forms its southeast border, Smyrna sits to the north and Austell to the west. The Silver Comet Trail, a 61.5-mile paved path starting in Smyrna, crosses Floyd Road in Mableton.

The area was once Cherokee and Creek land. A railroad station opened in December 1881 and the post office followed in 1882, which turned Mableton into a commercial hub for rural Cobb. The town incorporated in 1912 and gave up its charter in 1916 after a flood overwhelmed its sewer system and residents pushed to share drainage costs across the county. For more than a century afterward it was unincorporated, until the 2022 vote restored it.

The Cobb County School District runs the public schools. Elementary options include Mableton, Clay-Harmony Leland, Bryant, Riverside, Russell and City View, with Floyd, Garrett, Lindley and Betty Gray among the middle schools. Pebblebrook and South Cobb are the high schools named for the area. The South Cobb Regional Library serves the community, and private options include The SAE School for preschool through eighth grade.

School assignment follows your address, so confirm the zone with the district before you put a school name in a listing.

sections.h2: What new development is changing Mableton?
sections.html:
County planning documents describe a Mableton Town Center vision for the Mableton Parkway area, formalized after a 2010 design week and approved by the Cobb Board of Commissioners in 2013. Later projects included a 31-acre mixed-use plaza near Mableton Parkway and Old Powder Springs Road with townhomes, courtyard cottages and detached houses, and a 60-acre redevelopment along Floyd Road with apartments and townhomes approved on October 21, 2020.

For a seller, new construction nearby can raise buyer interest in the area while also giving buyers newer alternatives. Price against what is actually for sale on your street, not against the plan documents.

sections.h2: How are Mableton property taxes billed?
sections.html:
Mableton does not levy a general property tax, so Cobb County still bills county and school taxes, while the city bills special service districts separately. For 2026 the Cobb bills were issued in August and were due October 15, 2026. Cobb's assessor sets values at 40 percent of fair market value, and mailed 2026 assessment notices on June 5.

The city's Public Safety Special Services District covers the cost of police services the city took over from Cobb on June 1, 2025. The city began billing it in October 2026 at 4.5 mills, applied to the assessed value set by Cobb. A separate Six Flags Special Services District has been billed by the city since October 2025.

sections.h2: What does the new city tax mean at a closing?
sections.html:
Ask the closing attorney or title company to pull both the Cobb bill and the city district bills, because the city bill is separate and a buyer will want to know how it was handled. Your sales contract decides who covers which share of the year.

The city applies its millage to the assessed value that Cobb sets. Call the city finance office for the due date on its district bill, and keep proof of payment for the closing file. Homeowner relief also appears on Cobb bills: the 2026 announcement says the state's Homeowner Tax Relief Grant shows as a separate reduction for qualifying homeowners, and owners who no longer qualify for a homestead exemption must report it to the Tax Commissioner.

sections.h2: How do homestead exemptions work for a Mableton seller?
sections.html:
Cobb's assessor describes the exemption as a tax break for homeowners who live in the house as their primary residence, and for 2026 listed July 20 as the filing deadline. If you are no longer eligible, the assessor says you must report it before the appeal deadline, or you owe the unpaid taxes and interest plus a 50 percent penalty on the amount that was improperly reduced.

When you sell, tell the Tax Commissioner and your closing attorney that the house is no longer your primary residence from the date of transfer.

sections.h2: What permits and rules apply to Mableton houses?
sections.html:
The City of Mableton Building Division handles permits, reviews plans against Georgia minimum standard codes and issues Certificates of Occupancy. Applications must go through the online CloudPermit portal, and the division says not to email them. Construction work is allowed from 7 AM to 7 PM Monday through Friday and 9 AM to 5 PM on Saturday, with none on Sundays or designated holidays.

  • Gather permits and final inspection sign-offs for any recent work.
  • Have the general contractor confirm inspections were scheduled and passed.
  • If the home was rented, ask the city's Business License office whether any registration is still active.

sections.h2: What does Georgia charge to transfer a deed?
sections.html: The Georgia Department of Revenue prints the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100 of the sale price. The seller is liable unless the contract moves it to the buyer, and the Clerk of Superior Court will not record the deed until it is paid.

faqs.q: Does the City of Mableton charge property tax?
faqs.a: It does not levy a general property tax. It bills special service districts: a Public Safety district at 4.5 mills, begun in October 2026, and a Six Flags district, billed since October 2025. Cobb County still bills county and school taxes.

faqs.q: When were Cobb property taxes due for Mableton owners in 2026?
faqs.a: October 15, 2026. Payments had to be received by the Tax Commissioner's Office or postmarked by USPS by that date to count as on time.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date on the Cobb Notice of Assessment. The city says a parcel with a pending appeal gets a temporary bill at 85 percent of the assessed value until the appeal is final.

faqs.q: Does Cobb County still assess property values in Mableton?
faqs.a: Yes. The city says property values are set by Cobb County, and appeals go to the Cobb Board of Tax Assessors. Cobb also bills county and school taxes.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Mableton house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell as is to a buyer who accepts the condition, or fix items first and list. Gather any permit records for earlier work so a title search or inspection does not stall the closing.
